newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ANZ says it's big enough to be independent.
newsitem.headline: ANZ says it's big enough to be independent.

text.p: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd (ANZ) said on Wednesday it believed that it was big enough and had sufficient growth to continue as a successful and independent bank.

National Australia Bank (NAB) managing director Don Argus said earlier this month that the government's ban on mergers between Australia's four major banks meant that NAB and the other three big banks were vulnerable to foreign takeover.
But ANZ chairman Charles Goode said in a statement accompanying the bank's half year results that its international banking network was of immense value to the bank and Australia.

"We remain of the view that ANZ is of sufficient size and has sufficient growth and efficiency opportunities ahead of it to continue to be a successful and independent bank and reward shareholders well," Goode said.

"We consider our international banking network, particularly in Asia where we support the expansion of Australia's international trade and investment interests, to be of immense value to the bank and the nation," he said.
Goode said the recent review of the Australian financial services industry by the Wallis inquiry produced a sensible document which focused on the key issues.
The government has said competition in the banking sector must spread and deepen before it would sanction a major bank merger.
Apart from NAB and ANZ, the other major Australian banks are Westpac Banking Corp and Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
